questions.question: What is the first step that happens when you type a domain name like example.com into a browser?
options: DNS translates the name into an IP address
TCP breaks the page into packets
The router assigns a new IP address
questions.rationale: Before any request is sent, DNS resolves the human-friendly name to the server's numeric IP address.

questions.question: Why does the Internet use packet switching instead of sending data whole?
options: Packets can take different routes, so traffic survives path failures
It removes the need for addresses
It guarantees every packet arrives in order
questions.rationale: Chopping data into independently routed packets makes the network robust — if one path fails, others carry the traffic.

questions.question: Which protocol guarantees ordered, complete delivery and is used for web pages and email?
questions.rationale: TCP retransmits losses and restores order. UDP just sends without promises, suiting video calls and games.

questions.question: A home Wi-Fi network is an example of a:
questions.rationale: A LAN (local area network) covers a building or campus, like a home or office network; WANs span countries or the world.

questions.question: During a video call that keeps freezing while downloads run fast, which quantity is most likely the problem?
questions.rationale: Calls depend on low latency (how long one packet takes). High latency causes freezes even when bandwidth is plentiful.

questions.question: Which network type covers a whole city, such as a cable network?
questions.rationale: A MAN (metropolitan area network) spans a city — e.g., a cable network; WANs span countries or the world.

questions.question: In the client–server model, what is the role of the client?
options: It stores all web pages permanently
It assigns IP addresses to servers
It requests a resource from the server
questions.rationale: The client (your browser) requests a resource and the server responds with it — e.g., an HTTP request answered with HTML.

questions.question: Besides the data itself, what does each packet carry?
options: The full contents of every other packet
questions.rationale: Each packet is a small chunk carrying source/destination addresses and sequence numbers so it can be routed and reassembled at the destination.

questions.question: Which network layer handles delivery over one physical hop using technologies like Ethernet or Wi-Fi?
questions.rationale: The Link layer's job is delivery over one physical hop (Ethernet, Wi-Fi); the Internet layer does routing between hosts with IP.

questions.question: Which of these is given as an example of a PAN?
options: Bluetooth headset connected to a phone
questions.rationale: A PAN covers just a few metres — like a Bluetooth headset paired to a phone.
